chapter_title: Part 2 reprints Charles Murray’s follow-up essay, Underclass: The
text: Origins The concept of the ‘underclass’ does not originate with Murray, nor do all who deploy it share Murray’s understanding of its nature and causes.3 The term was coined in the US and was popularised there in the early 1980s by the journalist Ken Auletta who emphasised the behaviour and values of those deemed to be members of the ‘under- class’, though without claiming that these were necessarily the cause of their plight.

Origins
The concept of the ‘underclass’ does not originate with Murray, nor
